# Psalm 143 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A Psalm of David. Hear my prayer, O LORD; give ear to my pleas for mercy! In your faithfulness answer me, in your righteousness!

**2** Enter not into judgment with your servant, for no one living is righteous before you.

**3** For the enemy has pursued my soul; he has crushed my life to the ground; he has made me sit in darkness like those long dead.

**4** Therefore my spirit faints within me; my heart within me is appalled.

**5** I remember the days of old; I meditate on all that you have done; I ponder the work of your hands.

**6** I stretch out my hands to you; my soul thirsts for you like a parched land. Selah

**7** Answer me quickly, O LORD! My spirit fails! Hide not your face from me, lest I be like those who go down to the pit.

**8** Let me hear in the morning of your steadfast love, for in you I trust. Make me know the way I should walk, for to you I lift up my soul.

**9** Deliver me from my enemies, O LORD! I have fled to you for refuge.

**10** Teach me to do your will, for you are my God! Let your good Spirit lead me on level ground!

**11** For your name's sake, O LORD, preserve my life! In your righteousness bring my soul out of trouble!

**12** And in your steadfast love you will cut off my enemies, and you will destroy all the adversaries of my soul, for I am your servant.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 143.

- **143:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **143:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **143:5** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **143:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **143:9** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **143:11** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **143:2**: 'Not will-be-justified before-you any living' — the most explicit OT statement of universal human sinfulness; quoted by Paul in Romans 3:20 and Galatians 2:16.
- **143:10**: 'Your-Spirit good lead-me in-land level' — one of the rare OT references to God's Spirit as personal guide.

### LOGOS
- **143:2**: This verse is foundational for Paul's doctrine of justification by faith: no human being can be declared righteous before God on the basis of their own merit.
- **143:8**: 'Let me hear in the morning of your steadfast love' — the prayer for morning grace; each new day begins with the need to hear God's love again.

### PNEUMA
- **143:2**: This verse demolishes all self-righteousness: 'No living person is innocent before you.' Paul built his entire theology of grace on this single line.
- **143:6**: 'My soul is like cracked, dry earth thirsting for you.' That's what spiritual desperation feels like — parched, cracked, empty, needing God like the ground needs rain.

— SOPHIA
